text:
maria: Hey team, running into weird SSE behavior in the JS sample app — when the auth token refreshes mid-stream we occasionally get JSON parse errors because chunks arrive out of order. Repro steps below.

sam: ugh, that sounds like chunk-reassembly. Is this on hosted or dedicated?

maria: Hosted API (staging). JS SDK v2.3.1, sample-app (nextjs) using EventSource polyfill. I can repro reliably by forcing token expiry at ~30s into a long stream.

kevin: do you have raw SSE logs? the framing should be client-side reassembly, but auth refresh may abort and reconnect. If reconnect merges fragments incorrectly, that would do it.

maria: pasted a minimal log (trimmed):

```
[data] data: {"id":"msg-1","text":"hello wo"
[data] data: {"id":"msg-1","text":"rld"}

[data] data: {"id":"msg-2","text":"next"}
```

But sometimes when the auth refresh happens we get: 
```
[data] data: {"id":"msg-1","text":"hello "
[data] data: {"id":"msg-2","text":"next"}
[data] data: {"id":"msg-1","text":"world"}
```

Which ends up parsed as msg-2 and then a broken msg-1 fragment chopped onto it -> JSON error.

yuki: interesting. Do you see different last-event-id or resume token between connections?

maria: The server sends a resume-token header on reconnect (we recently added that). But the JS polyfill doesn't preserve ordering when it reattaches — it just emits events as data arrives; if two connections run concurrently during a quick reconnect the interleaving happens.

sam: Could be race: old connection not fully closed before auth refresh triggers new connection. Are you seeing any aborted sockets?

maria: yes, chrome network shows the old socket FIN, but there's overlap of ~200ms. We also saw a case where the polyfill replayed a cached chunk plus new stream chunk and they got concatenated by the parser.

kevin: Minimal workaround: 1) ensure client waits for explicit close before opening new EventSource during auth refresh, or 2) add per-fragment seq numbers at server to let client reorder. Which is easier to ship?

maria: For quick DX fix we can make the client delay re-open until confirm close. But longer term we should make server add fragment_seq and last_event_id semantics so SDKs can reassemble reliably.

yuki: Agree. Also SDK should buffer incomplete JSON fragments until boundary or a sequence gap. I'll open an issue: add "fragment_seq" metadata to SSE data envelope plus unit tests that force auth refresh mid-stream.

sam: Can you share a repro script? I can try to reproduce locally without hitting staging.

maria: Yep, repro below (node):

```
// repro.js
const EventSource = require('eventsource');
const es = new EventSource('https://staging.api.redwood.com/stream?force_long=true');
es.onmessage = (e) => { try { const d = JSON.parse(e.data); console.log('MSG', d); } catch (err) { console.error('PARSE ERR', e.data, err); }};
// after 25s, force token refresh in the sample app or hit /auth/refresh to simulate
```

kevin: thanks — i'll run it with a proxy that simulates 200ms overlap to stress race.

dev-bot: deploy-bot: new build for sample-app with SDK v2.3.2 pushed to staging (includes debug logs for SSE fragments). :rocket:

maria: quick status update — adding a client-side guard (ensure old ES closed before new open) eliminated the repro for me locally. Staging still flaky for some users though; I think we need server-assisted ordering.

sam: proposal for fix plan:
- short-term: ship client guard in JS SDK and note in sample app onboarding (avoid auth refresh mid-stream)
- mid-term: server embed fragment_seq + resume-token semantics; SDKs use seq to reassemble and detect gaps
- tests: add e2e harness that forces auth refresh with variable overlap (0-500ms) and validates final JSON order

yuki: I'll add the e2e harness and tests. Also request adding a small migration: keep last_event_id consistent across reconnects.

kevin: also add a telemetry flag when parse errors occur so we can detect customer impact.

maria: filed issues: devex#432 (js-sdk guard), infra#212 (sse fragment seq), e2e#109 (auth-overlap tests). I'll link PRs. Thanks! :thumbsup:
